newsitem.title: FRANCE: Usinor 96 cash flow 7.8 pct of sales.
newsitem.headline: Usinor 96 cash flow 7.8 pct of sales.

text.p: French steelmaker Usinor Sacilor said on Tuesday that cash flow in 1996 totalled 5.54 billion francs, representing 7.8 percent of sales revenues versus 10.3 percent in 1995.
It said industrial investments in 1996 resulted in 3.94 billion francs in outlays compared with 3.02 billion in 1995.

That, it said in a statement, reflected the advance in certain large projects such as the Sollac coke plant in Dunkirk and J&L's continuous cold rolling line in the United States. But it said the figure was still less than the depreciation expense for 1996 of 4.18 billion francs.

It added that considering the sharp drop in working capital requirements, cash provided by operations "amply covered all expenses of investment as well as the dividend payment for the 1995 results and enabled a very significant further reduction in the net financial debt."
Net debt fell to 6.5 billion francs from 11.0 billion.
The 1996 dividend payout of three francs per share, down from four francs in 1995, represented 49 percent of the net profit, it said.
